+## Exact conjecture direction and scope to audit
+
+In the 2020 paper's Discussion, “Identifiability of MSci Models,” the authors propose sequence-data identifiability **“as long as it is identifiable when the data consist of gene trees with coalescent times”**. The surrounding paragraph specifies multiple sequences from each species at each locus and multiple sites per locus. The [2022 paper](https://academic.oup.com/mbe/article/39/5/msac083/6568285), immediately before its Theory section, repeats the equivalence and says **“We make use of this conjecture”**; that is not a proof of the converse observation bridge.
+
+Write I_G for parameter identifiability from the relevant timed-genealogy distribution and I_X for identifiability from sequence-alignment distributions. The research direction is I_G => I_X. With a fixed common sequence channel, equality of the latent distributions implies equality of the observed distributions, so I_X => I_G is the easier information-loss direction. The difficult implication says that this channel loses no parameter distinction in the declared model family.
+
+The source does not provide a universal numerical finite locus-length cutoff in that paragraph. A result using unbounded within-locus length must not be substituted for a fixed-length claim. Before selecting a theorem, fix locus lengths versus number of independent loci, sample multiplicities, substitution/clock parameters and mutation-unit scale, and which genealogy/route labels are marginalized or identified. This remains a conjecture-scope and latest-prior audit, not a claimed new theorem or proof promise.
